claims.claim: All human activities are conditioned by human togetherness, but only action exclusively depends upon the constant presence of others.
claims.supporting_excerpt: All human activities are conditioned by the fact that men live together, but it is only action that cannot even be imagined outside the society of men.

claims.claim: The translation of Aristotle's zōon politikon as animal socialis reflects a loss of the original Greek understanding of politics.
claims.supporting_excerpt: More than any elaborate theory, this unconscious substitution of the social for the political betrays the extent to which the original Greek understanding of politics had been lost.

definitions.definition: Human life in so far as it is actively engaged in doing something, always rooted in a world of men and man-made things.

distinctions.distinction: A sharp distinction in a citizen's life between private existence and communal existence corresponding to the household versus the city-state.

segment_function: Introduction of Chapter II, discussing the relation between the vita activa and human togetherness, and examining the translation and historical evolution of animal socialis versus zōon politikon.
